title: Solve it together: keep the passing scores
idea: GUIDED (UEPCC). Use a True/False helper inside a loop to filter a list into a new one.
problem: is_pass(score) returns score >= 50. From [40, 70, 55, 30], build a list of only the passing scores.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: is_pass(score) returns score >= 50. From [40, 70, 55, 30], build a list of passing scores.

What is the OUTPUT?
options: A new list containing only the scores that pass
exercises.explanation: Output is a new, shorter list of just the passing scores. Name the output first.

exercises.prompt: What does the helper is_pass hand back for each score?
options: True or False (whether the score passes)
exercises.explanation: is_pass returns a boolean. We use that True/False to decide whether to keep the score.

exercises.prompt: Example by hand. Which of [40, 70, 55, 30] are >= 50?
exercises.explanation: 70 and 55 pass; 40 and 30 don't. So the kept list should be [70, 55].

exercises.prompt: A filtered list can be shorter than the original — that's expected.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Only passing items are kept, so [40, 70, 55, 30] becomes [70, 55].

blocks: For each score, if it passes, append it
exercises.explanation: Init empty list, loop appending only passers, then show. The helper supplies the pass/fail test.

exercises.prompt: What gets appended when is_pass(score) is True?
exercises.explanation: Append the actual score. The boolean only decides WHETHER to append; the item is what we keep.

exercises.prompt: Code it: define is_pass, empty list, loop with if, append, print.
exercises.explanation: Define the test, start kept empty, loop appending s only when is_pass(s) is True, then print [70, 55].
append s when the helper is True. kept becomes [70, 55].

exercises.prompt: Check — the code prints [70, 55]; your example said [70, 55]. So...
exercises.explanation: Output matches the hand-worked list, so the filter is correct.
Only 90 is >= 50, so kept is [90]. Works for new inputs too.
